newsitem.title: USA: Wyle Electronics sees Q1 below yr-ago Q1.
newsitem.headline: Wyle Electronics sees Q1 below yr-ago Q1.

text.p: Wyle Electronics said earnings for its first quarter will likely be lower than its 1996 fourth quarter, as well as below the first quarter a year ago.
The company said it anticipates a decline in first quarter earnings of between 15 to 20 percent from the 1996 fourth quarter.
Wyle reported 1996 fourth quarter earnings of $0.74 per share on sales of $316 million. It reported earnings of $0.86 per share on sales of $327 million for the first quarter a year ago.

"We are seeing generally positive business trends during the first quarter, as evidenced by our solid incoming orders for semiconductor products. At the same time, we're working through some specific issues unique to transitions in both our product and services mix," company president Ralph Ozorkiewicz said.

"As previously reported, we have been experiencing the effect of a transitioning product line, particularly during this quarter. We continue to ramp up shipments from our new National Semiconductor and Fairchild lines, after winding down our distribution agreements with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Philips Semiconductor earlier this quarter. During last year's fourth quarter, Wyle shipped a total of $18 million of AMD and Philips products," Ozorkiewicz said.
"In addition, the first quarter consists of two less shipping days than the fourth quarter, further affecting the sequential sales comparison.

"While we're achieving growth in other product areas to help offset these factors, the majority of such replacement revenue is being generated in lower margin lines that will negatively impact our first quarter margins." Ozorkiewicz said.
